history.historicalImportance: Buxar is historically significant for the Battle of Buxar (1764), which established the British East India Company's dominance in eastern India. The district is also closely associated with ancient Hindu traditions and the Ramayana.
history.formationHistory: Buxar district was carved out of the erstwhile Bhojpur district on 17 March 1991.
history.freedomMovement: The people of Buxar actively participated in the Indian freedom movement, including the Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement and Quit India Movement.
history.archaeologicalImportance: The district contains several ancient temples, archaeological sites and historical remains connected with the Battle of Buxar and the Ramayana.
historicalTimeline: Ancient period – Part of the Magadha Kingdom
Mythological period – Associated with Sage Vishwamitra and Lord Rama
1764 – Battle of Buxar fought between the British East India Company and the combined forces of Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II, Nawab of Awadh and Mir Qasim
17 March 1991 – Buxar district was formed after bifurcation from Bhojpur district

geography.location: Buxar district is located in the western part of Bihar along the banks of the Ganga River and shares its western boundary with Uttar Pradesh.

boundaries.north: Ballia (Uttar Pradesh) across the Ganga River

geography.climate: Subtropical climate with hot summers, monsoon rains and cool winters.
geography.forests: Very limited forest cover, mainly scattered plantation and riverine vegetation.

specialEconomicFeatures: Strategic location on the Bihar–Uttar Pradesh border

agriculture.dairyDevelopment: Dairy farming is an important source of rural livelihood, supported by milk cooperative societies.
agriculture.fisheries: Fish farming is practiced in ponds, rivers and irrigation canals across the district.

infrastructure.roadNetwork: Buxar has a well-developed road network connecting all major towns and villages through national highways, state highways and district roads.
infrastructure.airConnectivity: The nearest airport is Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport, Patna (about 125 km).
infrastructure.publicTransport: Bihar State Road Transport Corporation (BSRTC), private buses, taxis and auto-rickshaws provide transport services.
infrastructure.electricity: Most urban and rural areas have electricity connectivity under the state power distribution network.
infrastructure.waterSupply: Urban areas receive piped water supply while rural areas depend on hand pumps, tube wells and rural water supply schemes.
infrastructure.internetConnectivity: 4G and 5G mobile services are available in most parts of the district, with broadband connectivity in urban areas.

education.governmentSchools: More than 1,800 government primary, middle and secondary schools are functioning across the district.
education.privateSchools: Several CBSE, ICSE and Bihar Board affiliated private schools operate in Buxar district.
colleges: M.P. High School and College Campus, Buxar

healthcare.primaryHealthCentres: Primary Health Centres (PHCs) are functioning across all blocks of the district.
healthcare.ambulanceServices: 102 and 108 ambulance services are available throughout the district.

cultureAndHeritage.traditionalDress: Men traditionally wear Dhoti-Kurta and women wear Saree and Salwar-Kameez.
culturalOrganizations: District Art and Culture Office, Buxar
Department of Art, Culture and Youth, Bihar

sportsAcademies: Bihar State Sports Authority Training Centre
sportsAchievements: District athletes regularly participate in Bihar state-level competitions
School and college teams represent Buxar in various sports events
Growing participation in cricket, kabaddi and athletics

bankingAndFinance.atms: ATMs of major public sector and private sector banks are available across the district.
bankingAndFinance.digitalBanking: UPI, Internet Banking, Mobile Banking and AEPS services are widely available.
financialInclusionPrograms: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana

governanceAndPublicServices.districtAdministration: Buxar district is administered by the District Magistrate (DM) with support from various district-level departments.
governanceAndPublicServices.policeAdministration: Law and order is maintained by Buxar District Police under the Bihar Police.
governanceAndPublicServices.fireServices: Fire stations operate in Buxar and Dumraon to provide emergency fire and rescue services.
governanceAndPublicServices.publicDistributionSystem: Essential commodities are distributed through Fair Price Shops under the Public Distribution System (PDS).
eGovernanceServices: Bihar Right to Public Services Portal

lawAndOrder.trafficPolice: Traffic Police regulate traffic and road safety across the district.
lawAndOrder.disasterManagement: The District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA), Buxar coordinates disaster preparedness, flood management and emergency response.

environment.forestCover: Limited forest cover, mainly along the Ganga and Kaimur fringe areas.

mediaAndCommunication.postalServices: India Post provides postal, Speed Post, parcel and banking services across Buxar district.
mediaAndCommunication.telecommunication: 4G and 5G mobile connectivity is available in most urban and rural areas of the district.
